ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, in quadrilateral $ABCD$, $AB \parallel DC$ and $AB=DC$. The diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at point $O$. $AC$ bisects $\angle BAD$, and a line is drawn from point $C$ perpendicular to $AB$, intersecting the extension of $AB$ at point $E$. Line $OE$ is then drawn. Quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a rhombus. If $AB = \sqrt{10}$ and $BD = 2$, what is the area of $\triangle AOE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: \textbf{Solution:} Thus, the area of $\triangle AOE$ is $\boxed{\frac{27}{10}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In quadrilateral $ABCD$, $AB \parallel DC$ and $AB=DC$. The diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at point $O$. $AC$ bisects $\angle BAD$, and a line is drawn from point $C$ perpendicular to $AB$, intersecting the extension of $AB$ at point $E$. Line $OE$ is drawn. Quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a rhombus. If $AB = \sqrt{10}$ and $BD = 2$, what is the area of $\triangle AOE$?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, A, B, E are located on the same horizontal straight line, and E is to the right of B; D, C are above and DC is a horizontal line, AB is parallel to DC; from C a perpendicular is drawn downward to the extension line of AB and intersects at E, and a right angle is marked at E in the figure; diagonals AC and BD intersect at O, and OE is also drawn. The figure corresponds to rhombus ABCD. Reasoning: By the coordinate method, let A=(0,0), B=(√10,0). Let D=(u,v). Because AB∥DC and AB=DC, C=(u+√10,v) can be taken, and the foot of the perpendicular E=(u+√10,0). The side length of the rhombus AD=AB=√10, therefore u^2+v^2=10. Also BD=2, so (u-√10)^2+v^2=4. Subtract the two equations: [(u-√10)^2+v^2]-(u^2+v^2)=4-10, that is -2√10u+10=-6, obtaining 2√10u=16, so u=8/√10=4√10/5. Substitute into u^2+v^2=10, getting v^2=10-(4√10/5)^2=10-160/25=18/5=90/25, so v=3√10/5. Thus E=(u+√10,0)=(9√10/5,0). The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other, therefore O is the midpoint of AC, O=((9√10/5)/2,(3√10/5)/2)=(9√10/10,3√10/10). Triangle AOE takes AE as the base, AE=9√10/5; the height from O to AE is 3√10/10. Area = 1/2·(9√10/5)·(3√10/10)=27/10.
